pages.text: “Silver buds unfold, jade dew emits fragrance, unprocessed and pure in its natural essence.”$(br2)White tea is renowned for its most primitive and natural processing method. Unlike green and black tea, white tea undergoes minimal rolling or fermentation, relying solely on natural drying to preserve its purest flavor. Its infusion is clear and elegant, with a lingering sweet aftertaste, earning it the title of ‘Fairy of Teas.’

White tea thrives in warm and humid hilly and forested regions, with the highest quality found at high altitudes. Its tender buds are covered with fine silvery hairs, giving them a distinctive white appearance. Travelers seeking to cultivate white tea can search for wild tea trees or use white tea seeds to establish a tranquil tea garden.

White tea plants have strict environmental requirements, preferring warmth and humidity but showing greater cold resistance than green tea.$(br)The plant has a longer growth cycle, with each harvest yielding a small number of tender buds and a chance to drop additional white tea seeds for further expansion. Since white tea undergoes no rolling or fermentation, it can be brewed directly after drying, producing a delicate and refreshing taste.
